jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer, Physical AI Infrastructure
jobs.jd: About Nebius : Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure. Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI. Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D. The role Nebius is hiring a Forward Deployed Engineer to work alongside Physical AI customers, shape our core infrastructure products, and test ideas for what we should build next. You will work with enterprises, ISVs, and digital-native companies running training, simulation, synthetic data, evaluation, and model serving workloads. By understanding their systems and helping them reach production, you will uncover requirements that inform our Cloud, Serverless, and Token Factory teams. The goal is to connect needs across Physical AI industries with product decisions, including improvements that benefit enterprise customers more broadly. You will also investigate opportunities for new Nebius products. You will develop hypotheses about unmet needs, examine demand and existing alternatives, and build prototypes to test with customers. Your findings will help determine which opportunities deserve investment and what an initial product should deliver. The work is hands-on. You will write code, deploy and benchmark models, build agents, and troubleshoot infrastructure alongside customer engineers. The position is part of the Physical AI go-to-market team, with close collaboration across customers, NVIDIA, Product, and Engineering. What you will do Work with customer engineers to understand their workloads, infrastructure constraints, and production requirements. Translate Physical AI use cases into requirements that Cloud, Serverless, and Token Factory teams can use, backed by measurements and customer evidence. Identify enterprise adoption barriers and common needs across industries. Work with Product and Engineering to assess gaps and test improvements with customers. Build agents that set up, run, and debug Physical AI workloads, connecting them to clusters, schedulers, storage, and model servers. Deploy and benchmark open-weight models with serving stacks such as vLLM or SGLang, then tune them for customer workloads. Build prototypes and run technical evaluations to answer specific questions about performance, reliability, and product fit. Assess demand and existing alternatives for opportunities outside current product teams’ scope, then build where there is a clear market. Debug across Python, agents, model servers, Kubernetes, GPUs, networking, and storage. Turn successful setups into reusable scripts, deployments, and short guides. What we are looking for Three or more years in software engineering, cloud infrastructure, DevOps, ML infrastructure, or similar, including ownership of a production service, cluster, or platform. Experience working directly with customers or external engineers to scope problems, run evaluations, and explain technical tradeoffs. Ability to turn an unfamiliar customer problem into concrete infrastructure requirements. Practical experience building with LLMs or agents, at work or independently, with an understanding of their internals (e.g., transformers, KV caching, or tool calling) and how to evaluate their outputs. Familiarity with enterprise infrastructure requirements, including identity and access management, network isolation, security, monitoring, and reliability. Strong Python and Linux skills: you can read unfamiliar code, automate a setup, and debug from logs and metrics. Practical experience with containers and Kubernetes, including configuration, networking, storage, and scheduling. jobs.jd: L’histoire du groupe Theodo et son succès Theodo accompagne depuis 2009 les entreprises innovantes dans la conception, le développement et le déploiement de produits digitaux ingénieux - tels que la plateforme TF1+, l'application LCL Pro ou l'application France Identité Numérique - en tirant parti du meilleur de la technologie et de l’approche Lean. Theodo connait une croissance exceptionnelle depuis 15 ans : nos équipes rassemblent plus de 750 Theodoers, principalement des Software Engineers, passionnés de technologie et d’amélioration continue. En 2025, le groupe Theodo génère 100M€ de CA. Aujourd’hui, l’ambition du groupe est de se positionner comme le leader de l’IA appliquée au développement logiciel, c’est pourquoi nous avons lancé la practice AI Modernisation. Au sein de cette practice, nous accompagnons nos clients dans la modernisation de leurs systèmes legacy. Grâce à une IA maîtrisée et une méthode éprouvée, nous allons 3 fois plus vite sur le delivery de ces projets critiques. La practice accompagne principalement des scale-ups comme Qonto ou Doctolib et des grands groupes comme Carrefour, Pernod Ricard, Les Mousquetaires, Urgo, Cdiscount ou Edenred. Si tu veux rejoindre le futur de la tech, tu es au bon endroit ! Pourquoi on recrute un Forward Deployed Engineer ? Nos clients ont des systèmes legacy critiques, parfois vieux de 20 ans. Ils veulent les moderniser vite, sans casser ce qui marche. Pour y arriver, un bon outil IA ne suffit pas : il faut quelqu'un sur le terrain, au plus près des équipes du client, qui fait le lien entre leur réalité métier et nos agents et workflows IA. Le Forward Deployed Engineer est ce profil : à moitié ingénieur, à moitié consultant, et toujours responsable du résultat en production. Ton équipe : Tu rejoins la practice AI Modernisation et tu es détaché chez nos clients. Tu travailles avec un AI Architect, un Tech Lead, des Software Engineers et un Product Manager, et tu t'appuies sur une communauté tech de plus de 350 Theodoers : software engineers, tech leads, engineering managers et architectes. Tes futures missions Être en immersion chez le client : comprendre son métier, son SI, ses contraintes et ses équipes, et repérer où l'IA a le plus d'impact Déployer et adapter nos workflows IA (agents, LLM, outillage de migration) sur le code et l'infrastructure du client Coder au quotidien : prototyper vite, industrialiser, mettre en production, et ne pas t'arrêter tant que la valeur n'est pas constatée Accélérer la modernisation du legacy : cartographier, refactorer et migrer avec l'IA, avec un haut niveau de qualité (Clean Code, tests automatisés, code reviews) Faire monter en compétence les équipes du client : pair programming, revues de code, transmission des pratiques AI-native Être la voix du terrain : remonter aux équipes produit et aux architectes Theodo ce qui marche et ce qui bloque, pour améliorer nos outils et nos standards Contribuer au business : repérer de nouveaux cas d'usage chez le client et aider à construire les propositions Exemples de projets HealthHero : leader européen de la télémédecine, ils souhaitent moderniser leur plateforme française, Qare, en vue d'une fusion avec la plateforme UK. L'objectif est de passer de Loopback2 à Nest pour pouvoir upgrade de Node 10 vers Node 20. Grâce à notre méthode de modernisation accélérée par l'IA, nous passons d'une estimation à 70 semaines sans IA à une migration terminée en 21 semaines et accélérons la vitesse de delivery par 5. Pernod Ricard : modernisation d'une application interne de gestion des campagnes marketing, avec des millions d'euros en jeu. 23 semaines pour passer de Vue Express à React Nest, et connexion à leur nouvel ERP, auparavant impossible sans la migration. Ce que tu vas apprendre Devenir un ingénieur AI-native de haut niveau, capable de livrer avec l'IA sur des systèmes complexes en conditions réelles Développer une posture de conseil : cadrer un problème, convaincre des décideurs, piloter un changement Maîtriser tout le cycle, de la découverte du besoin jusqu'à la production Tes perspectives d'évolution Expertise : Tech Lead AI, AI Architect Avant-vente : Solution Architect Managériale : Engineering Manager Profil recherché Diplômé d'une top école d'ingénieur (Bac +5) 2 à 5 ans d'expérience en software engineering, idéalement en contexte client (conseil, ESN, startup en forte croissance) Une vraie pratique des LLM et des outils d'AI coding dans ton travail quotidien À l'aise sur une stack fullstack (Java / Spring Boot, Node / Nest, React / Next, Python) et curieux face aux environnements legacy Orienté client : tu aimes être sur le terrain, tu écoutes, tu reformules, tu sais dire non quand il le faut Ownership : tu te sens responsable du résultat, pas seulement du code Exigeant sur la qualité, tu sais arrêter la chaîne quand quelque chose ne va pas (#jidoka) Pédagogue, et excellente communication en français et en anglais Une méthodologie basée sur l'apprentissage continu Chez Theodo, nous avons construit notre approche tech autour d'une conviction forte : on développe d'abord les personnes, avant de développer les produits . Notre Lean Tech® System met l'accent sur l'apprentissage continu : tu évolueras dans un environnement qui investit sur le long terme, où l'objectif est de te permettre de progresser chaque jour. Pourquoi rejoindre Theodo ? L’environnement : 💼 Rejoindre un groupe de 750 personnes avec de nombreuses possibilités d’évolutions cross-entités 🤝 Chaque Theodoer est accompagné par un coach interne. Son objectif : t’épauler dans ton quotidien et parler objectifs de carrière via des séances de coaching hebdomadaires. 🎯 Participation à des projets associatifs grâce à la Fondation Theodo (Ada Tech School, Code Phoenix, Article 1…) 🎉 Soirées mensuelles, keynotes et week-end d’entreprise annuel Le package : 📈 Actionnariat salarié pour être associé à la réussite du groupe 💸 De l’épargne salariale avec un mécanisme d’intéressement en partenariat avec Epsor 🖥

jobs.jd: About the Team The Collective Alignment (User Signals) team is a post-training research team working at the intersection of data science, human feedback, and reinforcement learning. We develop methods for learning from real-world user interactions to build AI systems that deliver lasting value, helping people learn, grow, and accomplish increasingly complex goals with ChatGPT. Learning from user feedback presents fundamental research challenges: signals are often noisy, biased, and difficult to interpret, and improvements in offline metrics do not always translate into better experiences for users. Our team develops scientific approaches to understanding these signals and translating them into improvements in model behavior through evaluations, reward modeling, and post-training. About the Role As a Research Engineer or Research Scientist, you will investigate how AI systems can learn from human feedback and real-world usage to better serve users over time. You will develop new approaches to extracting meaningful learning signals from complex user interactions and incorporating those signals into model training. This role requires strong deep learning research skills, scientific rigor, and curiosity about how people interact with AI. You will design controlled experiments and ablations, critically examine the relationship between offline evaluations and online model behavior, and work closely with research, product, and data science teams to understand whether improvements translate into meaningful value for users. In this role, you will: - Develop novel methods for learning from human feedback and user interaction signals. - Research approaches to incorporating feedback into reward modeling, reinforcement learning, and post-training. - Design rigorous experiments and ablation studies to isolate the effects of new data, objectives, and training methods. - Develop offline evaluations and investigate their relationship with online experiments and real-world user outcomes. - Analyze unexpected results, investigate discrepancies between evaluation metrics and user behavior, and develop hypotheses to guide further research. - Evaluate tradeoffs and regressions to improve targeted model behaviors while preserving broader capabilities. - Collaborate with research, alignment, product, and data science teams. - Implement and debug experiments across large-scale deep learning research systems. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have a strong background in deep learning research through academic or industry experience. - Have demonstrated research ability through publications or substantive research contributions in deep learning or LLM post-training. - Have experience developing new machine learning methods and evaluating them through rigorous, hypothesis-driven experimentation. - Think critically about experimental design, measurement, and what evaluation results do and do not establish about model behavior. - Are comfortable designing ablations, investigating surprising results, and reasoning about the relationship between offline metrics and real-world outcomes. - Have strong programming skills and experience working with complex ML codebases. - Are curious about how people interact with AI and how those interactions can inform better models. Nice to have: - Experience with RLHF, reinforcement learning, or modern LLM post-training. - Research or demonstrated interest in AI alignment, human feedback, or user signals. - Experience with online experimentation, evaluation methodology, or learning from noisy and biased feedback. - Experience connecting machine learning research with real-world product behavior. jobs.title: Senior Applied Scientist, Demand Tech, Amazon Ads
jobs.jd: In Amazon Advertising, we apply machine learning at massive scale to optimize the prediction, ranking, and bidding behind every ad - deciding, in milliseconds, which ads to show shoppers and how to value them. We're looking for an experienced Applied Scientist to lead a science area within how we rank, value, and bid on ads for Amazon DVA+ (Display, Video, and Audio) - including how we judge whether an ad is a good fit for the page a shopper is on and for the shopper themselves. It's high-scale, low-latency, customer-facing science: your models run live in front of millions of shoppers under tight real-time constraints. The questions are genuinely open - how do you tell whether an ad is relevant to someone, how do you balance what's good for shoppers, advertisers, and Amazon, and how do you keep getting that right as shopping behavior and inventory shift underneath you? You'll set the technical direction for how we answer them, and have room to shape where we take it. A few things make this stand out: your models touch a huge share of the ads shoppers see every day, so even small improvements add up fast; you'll run modern ML live under strict latency limits, across regions and very different types of ad inventory; and the problem space is rich - from how we value and bid on ads, to keeping models stable as traffic shifts, to what makes an ad a good fit for a shopper. Key job responsibilities - Be the scientific point of reference for your area, mentoring scientists and engineers and raising the team's bar through code, design, and science review. - Shape the science roadmap for your area, aligning partner teams and building consensus across science and business. - Advance the state of the art in ranking, deep learning, and information retrieval, judging which problems are genuinely new versus solvable with existing approaches, and set the standards the team builds on. - Own ambiguous problems end to end with limited guidance: frame them, break them down for yourself and others, prototype, experiment, and ship. - Define how the team weighs competing objectives — shopper experience, advertiser and publisher value, and Amazon's business — and the metrics that keep models holding up across placements and marketplaces. - Write and ship your own production code, moving fast with modern AI coding assistants and agents — we're all builders here. A day in the life You might start by digging into last week's experiment results, then use an AI coding agent to get your next prototype built and ready to test in production. In the afternoon you could be sketching a new way to measure ad relevance, reading a recent paper that bears on it, and reviewing a teammate's design - as you are the person the team turns to when a problem gets hard. You'll move between hands-on science, writing and shipping real production code, setting the direction for your area, and helping the scientists and engineers around you do their best work. About the team We're a group of scientists and engineers based in Edinburgh and London, working to make Amazon's ads more performant and relevant. We sit within a larger team spread primarily across New York City and the UK, and we have a broad mandate to build and experiment. You'll lead a science area within that mandate, with the data and infrastructure to do the work well and room to grow your scope over time - including opportunities to attend top conferences (NeurIPS, KDD, ICML). - PhD or equivalent research experience - Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language - Experience in applied research - Experience in building machine learning models for business application - Experience with Machine and Deep Learning toolkits such as MXNet, TensorFlow, Caffe and PyTorch - PhD in machine learning, statistics, mathematics, physics, engineering, computer science, operations research, econometrics, optimization, or equivalent quantitative field. - Experience in recommender systems, performance advertising, or online auctions. jobs.title: Sr. Software Development Engineer – AI/ML Networking Disaggregated Inference, Annapurna Labs, Annapurna Labs
jobs.jd: Every token a large language model generates depends on data reaching the right accelerator at the right moment. As AI models outgrow any single chip, the network between accelerators becomes the bottleneck that decides how fast — and how affordably — the world's largest models can serve real users. That network layer is what our team builds. We're in search of an engineer to work at the frontier of disaggregated inference: splitting LLM serving into separate prefill and decode pools and moving the model's KV cache between them at the absolute limit of what the hardware allows. Get it right and users get answers in milliseconds; get it wrong and the fastest accelerators in the world sit idle waiting on data. You'll own pieces of the high-speed transfer path that make the difference, and you'll measure your success in how close you run to the theoretical peak of the machine. What we're looking for: Strong C/C++ and a love for low-level, performance-critical systems — solid command of Linux, kernels, memory, and writing fast code. The instinct to ask "how fast could this possibly go?" and the rigor to measure it. Experience with high-speed networking or HPC interconnects (RDMA, InfiniBand, libfabric, UCX, NIXL, MPI) is valued highly; embedded-systems experience is a plus. Prior AI/ML experience is welcome but not required — if you're a great systems engineer, we'll teach you the ML side. If you like solving genuinely hard problems, working shoulder-to-shoulder with HPC and ML customers, iterating fast, and shipping at a scale few places can offer, come join us. This is a role on the leading edge of AI/ML infrastructure. Key job responsibilities Build and optimize the low-level data-movement software across accelerators, servers, and heterogeneous memory — over AWS's highest-performance network fabric. Push performance to the hardware roofline: profile, find the real bottleneck, and close the gap between "it works" and "it runs as fast as physics permits." Work across the stack — from kernel and network transport up to the inference frameworks — and partner with teams building the chips, runtime, and models. Deliver features that run on our largest clusters, for our largest customers, serving the largest AI models in production. A day in the life Annapurna Labs, a crucial part of AWS, is responsible for developing hardware and software components for EC2 infrastructure. Our team focuses on building networking solutions that for Machine Learning (ML) and High-Performance Computing (HPC) workloads on AWS. We have mixed discipline orgs, you’d be working side by side with infrastructure experts, hardware engineers, RTL engineers, scientists & architects. Our workforce spans the globe and is truly international, you’ll find yourself working side by side with individuals from numerous countries. We take mentorship seriously, you can both expect senior mentorship and will be expected to mentor new and junior engineers. The pace is fast as we work on the latest advancements of AI/ML, but we take the time to bond as a team and enjoy the successes. We offer flexibility in working hours, and respect WLB as a core org tenet. The team enjoys working with numerous principal-level engineers and closely with directors, career growth opportunities are certainly available. This is a role where you will always be encouraged to keep learning, the AI/ML field is fast moving and constantly evolving. About the team You'd be joining Annapurna Labs, an integral part of AWS. Annapurna designs the hardware and software building blocks behind EC2 — every EC2 instance runs on hardware we designed. jobs.jd: AWS Applied AI Solutions (AAIS) is building toward a future where every business innovates with Amazon AI teammates. To get there, we build AI solutions that improve human capabilities and transform entire business functions. We create end-to-end products that surprise and delight out-of-the-box, making complex things easy and hard things possible, with no cloud experience required. We start with customers who embrace the future and build bridges to meet the rest where they are. We pursue ambitious opportunities with conviction, and we are looking for builders who share that mindset. The Team Join the next science revolution at AWS Life Sciences Applied AI Solutions where you'll work alongside world-class scientists to build AI that transforms how therapeutics are discovered, developed, and brought to patients. We're out to revolutionize how medicines are discovered, developed, and brought to patients powered by a new generation of AI. Our team tackles some of the hardest open problems at the intersection of frontier AI and life sciences. We apply biological foundation models large language models and agentic reasoning systems to life sciences problems then put them into the hands of customers as applications and managed services they can fine-tune tailor and deploy on their own data. The science challenges are deep: how do you design agentic systems that reason correctly over complex biological regulatory and clinical logic? How do you enable customers to tailor foundation models to their proprietary data and get better outputs with less effort? How do you adapt models to reason faithfully in high-stakes scientific and regulatory domains? Today we're focused on two areas. In clinical trials we're building AI that automates and optimizes regulatory and clinical development workflows. In drug design our products (including Amazon Bio Discovery) accelerate discovery by giving bench scientists AI-guided protein engineering and antibody design capabilities. We combine frontier research with production-scale delivery to put breakthrough science into the hands of customers solving humanity's hardest problems. We value scientific rigor encourage publication and support conference participation. If you want to do research that ships this is the team. You will work closely with senior and principal scientists on well-scoped research problems own your results end to end and see your work reach production. You will work on how large language models reason plan and act in complex scientific domains while applying domain knowledge to ensure models produce scientifically valid outputs. The problems span multiple fronts: • How do you build LLM-based agentic systems that correctly reason over clinical protocols regulatory standards and complex multi-step operational workflows? • How do you evaluate agent reliability and faithfulness rigorously enough to trust in high-stakes clinical settings? • How do you develop model customization methods (fine-tuning retrieval augmentation domain adaptation) that let customers get strong results from foundation models on their own data? jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Applications and Compiler Engineer, LPX
jobs.jd: We are now looking for a Senior Machine Learning Applications and Compiler Engineer! NVIDIA is seeking engineers to develop algorithms and optimizations for our LPX inference and compiler stack. You will work at the intersection of large-scale systems, compilers, and deep learning, crafting how neural network workloads map onto future NVIDIA platforms. This is your chance to be part of something outstandingly innovative! What you’ll be doing: Build, develop, and maintain high-performance runtime and compiler components, focusing on end-to-end inference optimization. Define and implement mappings of large-scale inference workloads onto NVIDIA’s systems. Extend and integrate with NVIDIA’s SW ecosystem, contributing to libraries, tooling, and interfaces that enable seamless deployment of models across platforms. Benchmark, profile, and monitor key performance and efficiency metrics to ensure the compiler generates efficient mappings of neural network graphs to our inference hardware. Collaborate closely with hardware architects and design teams to feedback software observations, influence future architectures, and codesign features that unlock new performance and efficiency points. Prototype and evaluate new compilation and runtime techniques, including graph transformations, scheduling strategies, and memory/layout optimizations tailored to spatial processors. Publish and present technical work on novel compilation approaches for inference and related spatial accelerators at top tier ML, compiler, and computer architecture venues. Strong software engineering background with proficiency in systems level programming (e.g., C/C++ and/or Rust) and solid CS fundamentals in data structures, algorithms, and concurrency. Hands on experience with compiler or runtime development, including IR design, optimization passes, or code generation. Experience with LLVM and/or MLIR, including building custom passes, dialects, or integrations. Familiarity with deep learning frameworks such as TensorFlow and PyTorch, and experience working with portable graph formats such as ONNX. Solid understanding of parallel and heterogeneous compute architectures, such as GPUs, spatial accelerators, or other domain specific processors. Strong analytical and debugging skills, with experience using profiling, tracing, and benchmarking tools to drive performance improvements. Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work across hardware, systems, and software teams. Ideal candidates will have direct experience with MLIR based compilers or other multilevel IR stacks, especially in the context of graph based deep learning workloads. Ways to stand out from the crowd: Prior work on spatial or dataflow architectures, including static scheduling, pipeline parallelism, or tensor parallelism at scale. Contributions to opensource ML frameworks, compilers, or runtime systems, particularly in areas related to performance or scalability. Demonstrated research impact, such as publications or presentations at conferences like PLDI, CGO, ASPLOS, ISCA, MICRO, MLSys, NeurIPS, or similar. jobs.title: Research Engineer / Research Scientist, Human Flourishing
jobs.jd: About the Team The Human Flourishing team’s mission is to ensure AI systems understand and advance human flourishing. As AI becomes more capable and plays a larger role in people’s lives, we want its human benefits to grow with its capabilities. The Human Flourishing team is part of the broader Post Training organization. Our approach has two parts. Firstly, we measure and improve models’ understanding, capability, and propensity to act according to people’s values and to help them achieve their long-term goals. Secondly, we directly scale tangible impact for users in human domains like education and mental health, working across research, product, and partnerships to increase the benefits over a billion people experience weekly when they use ChatGPT. Our recent work includes Beneficial RL https://alignment.openai.com/beneficial-rl/, which investigates how training for beneficial behavior generalizes across settings, and MentalHealthBench https://openai.com/index/introducing-mentalhealthbench/, a benchmark developed with mental health experts to evaluate realistic conversations. About the Role We’re looking for an exceptional, hands-on researcher to turn difficult-to-define signals of long-term flourishing into measurable improvements in model behavior. You’ll help set research direction, build what is needed to test your ideas, and drive successful work into the models and products we ship. We’re especially interested in researchers with deep experience improving frontier models through pretraining or reinforcement learning (RL) / post-training, especially on less verifiable problems, or researchers who combine strong LLM skills with deep expertise in domains like education or mental health. Prior experience in these domains is not required. In this role, you will - Develop scalable training methods across the training stack that improve how models understand people’s values, support their agency, and help them achieve long-term goals. - Lead high-leverage research from an open question to a shipped improvement: choose a hard-to-define problem, iteratively define success, run experiments, and integrate into frontier models. - Build RL environments for difficult-to-verify outcomes, and study whether beneficial behavior generalizes across settings. - Create evaluations grounded in human expertise and feedback that reveal capability gaps, unintended incentives in RL, and failures that aggregate scores can miss. - Test whether measures of model behavior predict better learning, wellbeing, and other long-term outcomes, and use those findings to guide training. - Build new 0→1 capabilities in human domains that may have an increasing impact with upcoming increases in model intelligence and test-time compute. - Partner with product teams, engineers, partnerships teams, and domain experts to deploy promising methods, measure their effects in real use, and turn what you learn into further improvements. - Assess AI’s impacts on human flourishing at the scale of over a billion users. You might thrive in this role if you - Care deeply about helping AI improve people’s lives, and feel this is a responsibility that comes with increasingly capable models. - Have an unusually strong research record in pretraining or RL / post-training research, especially in a hard-to-verify area; or combine strong LLM research skills with deep expertise in education, mental health, or a related field of human benefit. - Are a hands-on builder who can turn ideas into rigorous experiments, write and debug code, and work directly with data and training infrastructure. - Have the taste to choose consequential problems and actionable steps on the path to solving those problems. - Take ownership of ambiguous problems and choose methods based on the impact they can deliver, including when the most useful work is unglamorous. - Care about whether a capability will scale, generalize, and make it into the real world—not just whether it can be shown in a paper or prototype. - Work well across disciplines and can grok the most important bottlenecks to scaling our impact in a multidisciplinary problem. If you’re excited about ensuring AI systems advance human flourishing, we’d love to hear from you. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. jobs.title: Senior Applied Scientist, Last Hundred Yards
jobs.jd: Every doorstep is different. Our robot has to understand all of them. We're building robots to deliver packages to customer homes. To make that possible, we're creating a system that can automatically generate a simulation-ready digital twin of the outdoor delivery environment for every customer home Amazon delivers to; modeling the driveways, yards, walkways, stairs, porches, and doorsteps a robot must understand and navigate. And the goal isn't simply to create virtual worlds that look real. They need to be real in the ways that matter to a robot. Geometry, semantics, appearance, physical properties, and the varied environmental cues that influence perception, planning, and motion, must be reproduced faithfully so robot behaviors from the field are repeatable in simulation. Our simulator becomes an effective tool to study the problem. The same autonomy software that runs on the physical robot also runs in simulation. When robot behavior differs between simulation and reality, we can ask why, and improve the representation, simulation, or models that produced the difference. Our North Star ambition is a system capable of modeling the delivery environment for every customer home we serve, across the enormous diversity of real residential environments. There isn't an established recipe for doing this. We are advancing the knowledge frontier of scene reconstruction. The right representation may combine classical geometry, learned scene representations, generative models, world models, or approaches that haven't been invented yet. We're interested in people with deep expertise in one or more areas of: Computer vision, 3D graphics, scene reconstruction, physics simulation, neural scene representations, Gaussian splatting, generative AI, world models, or related areas - with a strong interest in applying that expertise to robotics. Role Overview This is applied research with a short distance from idea conception to physical consequence. You'll work closely with robotics, autonomy, simulation, and software engineers to turn promising methods into systems that change how real robots perceive, plan, and navigate at Amazon scale. As a Sr. Applied Scientist on the Last Mile Robotics team, you will develop cutting-edge methods for capturing, reconstructing, and simulating real-world delivery environments in high-fidelity 3D. Your work will directly enable autonomous robots to understand and navigate the diverse conditions found at customer doorsteps. You will push the boundaries of scene reconstruction, neural rendering, and generative modeling, transforming scientific breakthroughs into physical impact through rapid experimentation and close collaboration with robotics, autonomy, and simulation teams. - Experience in applied research - Knowledge of programming languages such as C/C++, Python, Java or Perl Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. jobs.jd: Ekimetrics est un leader mondial de l'efficacité marketing et commerciale et des solutions d'IA à l'échelle. Depuis 2006, nous aidons les entreprises à optimiser leur marketing et leurs opérations en combinant IA avec expertise business et technologique dans 4 domaines : Marketing & commercial effectiveness, Customer analytics, Operational excellence, ESG & sustainability. Avec une équipe 100% internalisée et des bureaux à Paris, Londres, New York, Hong Kong et Shanghai, nous concevons des solutions sur mesure qui transforment les données en impact positif concret, grâce à une combinaison unique de technologie et de services. Notre force est de déployer une IA à impact, à grande échelle. Notre mission : mobiliser cette puissance pour répondre aux défis les plus urgents de notre temps. Nous nous engageons pour une IA responsable et frugale, pour garantir un impact constant à grande échelle, et pour rester fidèles à nos valeurs et à notre ADN. Contexte Les modèles marketing sont mis à jour à mesure que de nouvelles données arrivent : ventes hebdomadaires, résultats de campagnes, comportement des clients. Ils comprennent les marketing mix models (MMM), qui estiment le retour sur investissement de chaque canal média, ainsi que les modèles de demande et de promotion et les modèles de réponse client. Chaque mise à jour fait bouger les estimations, et la première question des métiers est : pourquoi ont-elles bougé ? Notre équipe a développé une méthode qui y répond de façon exacte pour les modèles bayésiens. Elle répartit le déplacement de toute quantité a posteriori entre des groupes d'observations : semaines, campagnes, régions, segments de clients ou expériences. La méthode est en cours d'évaluation par les pairs. Un premier prototype sur le MMM suit déjà une estimation semaine après semaine et lève une alerte quand une mise à jour la déplace plus que prévu. Sujet : pourquoi l'estimation a-t-elle bougé ? Attribution bayésienne en ligne pour les modèles marketing. Volet recherche (environ 3 mois) • Étendre l'attribution à l'apprentissage bayésien en ligne : mises à jour séquentielles, effets variables dans le temps (modèles linéaires dynamiques, filtre de Kalman), oubli des données anciennes. • Distinguer les trois causes d'un déplacement à chaque mise à jour : les nouvelles données, un vrai changement du marché et une erreur dans un flux de données. • Calibrer l'alerte de mise à jour : taux de fausses alertes et délai de détection, sur des données simulées dont la vérité est connue et sur des données publiques, pour le MMM et pour au moins un autre modèle marketing. • Rédiger un article destiné à un public de statistique ou de marketing science. Volet produit (environ 3 mois) • Transformer la méthode en un module Python testé, compatible avec nos outils de modélisation bayésienne (le MMM en premier). • Construire les sorties destinées aux métiers : une vue « ce qui a fait bouger l'estimation » et une alerte de mise à jour. • Les valider avec des consultants sur des cas réels, puis les documenter et les transmettre à l'équipe produit. Livrables attendus • Un article soumis à une revue ou une conférence à comité de lecture. • Un module Python testé et documenté, intégré à nos outils de modélisation. • Un guide court pour les consultants : comment lire et expliquer une attribution. Profil • Étudiant ou étudiante en dernière année de master ou d'école d'ingénieurs, en statistique, science des données ou probabilités. • Statistique bayésienne (prior, posterior, MCMC), et idéalement séries temporelles ou modèles à espace d'états. • Bonne maîtrise de Python (NumPy, une librairie de programmation probabiliste comme PyMC ou NumPyro), Git, tests unitaires. • Intérêt pour l'application de la statistique au marketing et pour l'explication des résultats à des non-spécialistes. Aucune connaissance préalable en marketing n'est requise. Rédaction claire en anglais. Pourquoi nous rejoindre ? Chez Ekimetrics, vos idées comptent vraiment et vous appartiennent — à vous de leur donner vie. Nous cultivons un esprit entrepreneurial qui vous encourage à repousser les limites pour créer un impact significatif. Mais il ne s’agit pas seulement de réussites individuelles : nous avançons ensemble, en nous enrichissant mutuellement. Ensemble, nous apprenons et progressons en continu , que ce soit à travers des parcours de carrière personnalisés, des projets stimulants, du mentorat, ou simplement grâce à la diversité des perspectives que chacun.e apporte. Et surtout, nous croyons au plaisir dans le travail. Ekimetrics est un environnement stimulant et bienveillant, où chacun.e peut s’épanouir en étant pleinement soi-même. En 2023, Ekimetrics a obtenu le statut d’entreprise à mission qui témoigne de notre ambition forte en matière de RSE. Notre raison d’être : Faire de la data science et de l’intelligence artificielle l’accélérateur de la transformation durable des organisations. Nous sommes également certifiés Great Place to Work© en France, au Royaume-Uni et aux Etats-Unis, et notre bureau de Hong Kong a reçu le prix Best Companies to Work for in Asia 2023©. Ekimetrics fait partie du classement French Tech 120 !Nous avons été sélectionnés par La French Tech pour rejoindre le prestigieux groupe des 120 scale-ups françaises les plus performantes, avec un fort potentiel pour devenir des leaders internationaux. Vous aurez accès : · Au catalogue de formation Eki.Academy qui contient des programmes qui vous feront monter en compétences sur nos solutions et nos métiers, des parcours apprenants sur notre plateforme digitale ainsi que des programmes dédiés à nos enjeux prioritaires, dont la sensibilisation aux sujets environnementaux avec la Climate School. · A une vie sportive, artistique, musicale, ludique, caritative et engagée : de notre salle de sport privatisée à nos expositions d’art, en passant par des jeux vidéo et des concerts, ou encore les défis RSE sur la plateforme Vendredi. jobs.title: Senior Applied Scientist, AWS Elemental
jobs.jd: AWS Elemental builds media services used by broadcasters, streaming platforms, and sports leagues to prepare, process, deliver, and monetize video. Elemental Inference is the applied machine learning team within that organization. We develop models that understand and transform live and file-based video, producing capabilities such as intelligent reframing, highlight detection, video enhancement, and contextual metadata for advertising and content discovery. Our work reaches customers through the same media workflows that carry major live events, always-on channels, and large on-demand libraries. As a Senior Applied Scientist, you will develop new machine learning approaches and carry the strongest ideas into production. Current work spans multimodal video, audio, and language models; spatial and temporal understanding; active-speaker and point-of-interest detection; scene retrieval; video super-resolution; and learned methods for improving compression. These problems rarely have a single accepted metric or a ready-made dataset. You will help define the task itself, determine what evidence is needed, and build evaluation methods that reflect the experience of people watching and working with the resulting video. This role combines applied research with the practical demands of a real-time media service. You will design datasets and objectives, train models at scale, run controlled comparisons, and investigate failures. You will also work closely with engineers to export, optimize, and deploy those models. A result is not finished when it performs well in a notebook. It must preserve its quality after conversion, fit within GPU memory, meet latency and throughput targets, handle the temporal behavior of live video, and operate at a cost customers can sustain. You will be a technical leader on the team as well as an individual contributor. The role calls for someone who can take an ambiguous customer problem, separate the scientific questions from the engineering constraints, and lead a team toward a defensible answer. You will review experiments and models, mentor other scientists and engineers, and improve the shared methods the team uses for training and evaluation. Strong judgment matters here. So does the ability to explain a complicated result clearly, including its limitations, to people from several disciplines. We welcome candidates with deep experience in computer vision, multimodal learning, video processing, or related areas. Direct media experience is valuable but not required. A scientist who has solved difficult problems in another field, understands how to test ideas rigorously, and wants to learn the video domain can also succeed in this role. Key job responsibilities Lead the formulation of ambiguous video problems into research plans with clear datasets, objectives, baselines, evaluation protocols, and production acceptance criteria. Develop models for multimodal video understanding and generation, spatial and temporal reasoning, detection and tracking, scene retrieval, video enhancement, and learned compression. Develop models for multimodal video understanding and description, spatial and temporal reasoning, detection and tracking, scene retrieval, video enhancement, and learned compression. Build evaluations that measure the behavior customers will see. Depending on the problem, this may include task accuracy, factual support, temporal localization, retrieval quality, perceptual video quality, rate-distortion performance, or human review. Take models from research code to production-ready artifacts. Partner with engineers on model export, reduced-precision inference, quantization, numerical parity, accelerator-specific optimization, and integration with serving systems and video pipelines. Balance model quality against latency, throughput, GPU memory, context limits, and operating cost. Diagnose problems across training stability, data quality, precision, compilation, serving, and live temporal behavior. Build reusable mechanisms for dataset management, experimentation, model comparison, regression detection, and performance measurement rather than solving each research problem in isolation. Review scientific work and production code. Identify weak comparisons, data leakage, unsupported conclusions, untested edge cases, and operational risks before they reach customers. Work with product managers, software engineers, and other scientists to make scope and design decisions. Use evidence to resolve disagreement and communicate what is known, what remains uncertain, and what further work is worth doing. Mentor scientists and engineers in experimental design, machine learning methods, video evaluation, and production ML practices. Contribute applied research through internal technical reports, patents, and publications at appropriate conferences or workshops. About the team AWS Elemental provides a portfolio of cloud media services built to prepare, process, deliver, and monetize video at global scale. Our technology supports some of the world's largest live broadcasts as well as 24/7 channels and on-demand content. The broader organization brings together expertise in video coding, image processing, distributed systems, advertising, and the operational demands of professional media. Elemental Inference applies machine learning across that video pipeline. The team works on video understanding and enhancement, contextual metadata, smart composition, event detection, retrieval, and compression. Some projects use large multimodal models that combine video, audio, and language. Others use specialized temporal or spatial models designed for a narrow task and a strict real-time budget. We choose the approach that fits the customer problem rather than forcing every problem into the same model family. Scientists on the team own more than model architecture. They build and govern datasets, develop annotation methods, train on distributed GPU infrastructure, and create evaluations

jobs.jd: As an Advisory Solution Consultant - CRM & Agentic AI for the Public Sector in Germany , you are the technical face of a fundamentally different way of selling. You partner with Sales, Product Management, and Executive Leadership to turn a single, well-chosen use case into undeniable, data-backed proof that earns the next phase of the relationship. This role blends the consultative instincts of a Sr. Advisory Solution Consultant with the hands-on, build-it-in-the-field engineering of a forward-deployed engineer: someone who works inside the customer’s own environment, configuring and proving solutions on their live data rather than presenting finished products from the outside. The Embedded Approach The Advisory Solution Consultant inverts the traditional pre-sales motion. The center of gravity is the POV: a short, focused cycle where we get access to a slice of the customer’s data, stand up an Agentic workflow against a problem they genuinely care about, and let the outcome speak for itself. Your job is to earn the right to that POV through rigorous Discovery, then deliver it as an embedded engineer, not a presenter. Build and deliver the POV as an embedded engineer — configuring Agentic workflows against the customer’s environment and producing measurable, data-backed results. Translate POV outcomes into an executive value narrative that quantifies impact and defines the path from a single proven use case to enterprise-wide adoption. Ensure every Discovery and POV engagement aligns with regional data privacy laws, security expectations, and enterprise compliance standards for handling customer data. jobs.title: Treasury, Trade Finance & Cash Flow Forecasting
jobs.jd: About the Team OpenAI Finance is responsible for ensuring the organization is set up for success in pursuit of its mission. The Treasury team is responsible for protecting liquidity, enabling scale, maintaining strong controls, and helping the company operate with clarity and resilience. We work across finance and operational partners to ensure funds move safely, visibility remains high, and Treasury infrastructure keeps pace with a fast-moving business. As hands-on operators and builders, we combine financial judgment with AI, automation, and data to solve problems faster, strengthen controls, and continuously improve how Treasury operates. About the Role We are looking for a senior hire to help structure financing for major deals, improve working capital, and lead cash forecasting and liquidity planning. Reporting to the Treasurer, you’ll partner with Compute and teams across OpenAI to design creative financing and payment solutions that support the company’s growth. AI and automation will be core to how you build and scale this capability. This role can be based in San Francisco, CA, Seattle, WA, or New York, NY. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. In this role, you will: - Structure and negotiate trade finance solutions that improve deal economics and manage risk. - Improve cash conversion by working with Billing, Collections, Accounting, and business teams to bill sooner, collect faster, improve supplier terms, and reduce unnecessary deposits or inventory commitments. - Free up cash and credit capacity by managing collateral, letters of credit, guarantees, and renewals. - Build direct cash forecasts by incorporating business-specific receipts and payments, compute commitments, and financing timing. - Partner with Treasury’s Investment team to determine liquidity buffers, investment decisions, and contingency funding plans. - Advise on deal structuring Compute, Finance, and Legal, then coordinate execution with Treasury Operations. - Improve e-commerce payment economics with Product, Payments, and Strategic Finance, balancing cost, acceptance, risk, and settlement timing. - Recommend billing, collection, prepayment, and credit terms for new business models, balancing cash protection with ease of purchase. - Use AI and automation to streamline contract review, credit support tracking, cash forecasting, and treasury workflows. You might thrive in this role if you have: - 10+ years of progressive experience in corporate treasury or banking, including trade finance structuring, working capital management, and cash flow forecasting. - A strong track record of negotiating and implementing complex trade finance across multiple instruments. - Experience delivering measurable cash conversion improvements through billing, collections, supplier terms, or inventory. - Sound judgment on contracts, risk, and approvals, and the ability to explain trade-offs to senior leaders and align business, finance, and legal teams. - Built direct cash flow forecasts and reconciled them to an indirect forecast or cash flow statement, with a strong grasp of how commercial terms and balance sheet changes affect liquidity. - Leveraged AI or automation to improve finance workflows end-to-end. - Experience in infrastructure, hardware, or other capital-intensive businesses, or familiarity with global e-commerce payments (preferred but not required).
